persona: Apparel art director for independent labels

designs.title: How Beer Is Made
designs.why: Clean, well-ordered and print-safe: solid line weights, readable headings, a clear S-shaped flow. But it reads as a brewery-tour infographic or textbook diagram, not a $50 graphic tee. The vessels are generic clip-art, the rounded geometric sans has no voice, and from 3 m it's a grid of small grey boxes with captions too small to read on a back. There's no hero image and no point of view.
designs.fix: Give it an identity. Add a strong title lockup ('HOW BEER IS MADE' in a characterful condensed or slab face, maybe with a faux brewery seal or edition line), cut the captions to just headings or drop them, and enlarge the drawings so the flow fills the back as one bold graphic instead of nine small cells.

designs.title: Gin Botanicals
designs.why: The strongest concept and the best fit for the market: an antique specimen-plate layout, with good subject choice and elegant italic Latin labels. It balances well on the white tee. Up close the 'engraving' falls apart. It's auto-traced, with broken contour lines, scattered speckle dots and blotchy fill in the juniper berries, orange peel and angelica root instead of real hatching. Inked, it will look like a degraded scan, not a fine engraving, and the specks risk dot gain and fill-in.
designs.fix: Redraw or clean the line art as true engraving: continuous contours with directional hatching and cross-hatching for tone instead of noise speckle, and a minimum line/dot size of about 0.3 mm. Keep the layout and type as they are.

designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: From 3 m it's the most striking image of the three: a nice tall, vignetted composition, cypresses and farmhouse as a clear focal point, terraces that lead the eye, and a refined spaced-serif 'VINEYARD.' that gives it a quiet premium feel. Up close it has the same trace artifacts as #2. The foreground vines and grapes are a dense mass of broken dashes and blobs with no tonal hierarchy, so they'll print as a dark muddy block and fight the focal point. The subject is also fairly generic Tuscan-postcard.
designs.fix: Clean up and simplify the foreground. Redraw the grapes and leaves with fewer, crisper lines and open more white space between rows, so tone builds from light hills to a controlled dark foreground. Replace speckle noise with real engraved line texture throughout.
